svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
DVWA · 3 components · 5 data flows · 4 trust boundaries · 51 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-04; tb-2 External → C-03; tb-5 C-04 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-4 C-04 → C-01

df-001: DVWA web application queries and writes MariaDB via mysqli (MySQL) df-001 authentication: Database user and password from configuration used in mysqli_connect; evidence: dvwa/includes/DBMS/MySQL.php:13

df-002: User submits username and password to login.php form (HTTP) df-002 authentication: login.php checks username and MD5 of password against the users table, with an anti-CSRF session token; evidence: login.php:39

df-003: Server posts CAPTCHA response, secret key and client IP to Google siteverify (HTTPS) df-003 authentication: reCAPTCHA secret key sent as the secret parameter; evidence: external/recaptcha/recaptchalib.php:14

df-004: Client posts JSON credentials to API login endpoint (HTTP) df-004 authentication: username and password in JSON body compared with fixed values in LoginController; evidence: vulnerabilities/api/src/LoginController.php:60

df-005: Client calls API order, user and health routes dispatched by URI path (HTTP) df-005 authentication: Front controller dispatches by path; authentication in the controllers was not read; evidence: vulnerabilities/api/public/index.php:51

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE category: filled = findings in that category
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
